clue.text: Consider route leading to summit, we're told

indicators.note: we're told signals that the phrase is heard rather than read, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: a route leading to a summit is the way up

explanation.surface: A climber mulls over the path to the top as it is described to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we're told' turns WAY UP into its soundalike.
explanation.definitionFit: To weigh up a situation is to assess or ponder it, a phrasal synonym of consider.

clue.text: Most astute, one's settled in our part of the world

indicators.note: settled in means placed within, so one's goes inside the region

parts.note: the West is our part of the world for a British setter
one's means one is: I for one, plus S

explanation.surface: The shrewdest person has made a home in the western world.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisest is the superlative of wise, meaning shrewdest, a synonym of most astute.

clue.text: Company he is performing with in winter spectacular?

indicators.note: performing suggests acting out, so the letters are put through a new routine

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A troupe member is on stage in a seasonal show.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice show is a spectacular on ice; the question mark admits winter as a playful nod to ice.

clue.text: Item of luggage journalist declares has been packed

indicators.note: has been packed means one word is stowed inside another, like goods in a bag

parts.note: a hack is a journalist, often a disparaging term
avers means declares or asserts

explanation.surface: A reporter announces that their bag has been filled.
explanation.definitionFit: A haversack is a bag carried on the back or shoulder, an item of luggage.

clue.text: Feeble joke with unfunny ending

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words

indicators.note: ending picks the last letter of the word unfunny

explanation.surface: A weak gag falls flat at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Puny means weak or small, a synonym of feeble.

clue.text: Girl, tense after card game

indicators.note: after places the abbreviation for tense behind the card game

parts.note: bridge is a card game for four players
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A girl grows tense after a hand of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridget is a girl's given name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: Double amount of audacity needed for hold-up

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or audacity
neck means cheek or audacity, as in having the neck to ask

explanation.surface: It takes twice the nerve to commit a robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double' means two words for audacity are needed; 'hold-up' is a delay, not a robbery.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottleneck is a narrow point causing delay, a hold-up in traffic.

clue.text: Minor figure from popular group

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a set is a group of things or people

explanation.surface: A bit-part player comes from a well-liked band.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is a small picture or diagram set within a larger one, a minor figure.

clue.text: Fool's comeuppance, perhaps short and sweet

indicators.note: comeuppance read as coming up: in a down clue the word for fool rises, read upwards

parts.note: a mug is a fool or dupe
a short is a drink of spirits, and a drop is one such small drink

explanation.surface: A fool gets just deserts, quick and painless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comeuppance' is read as come-up: in a down clue the fool rises. 'short and sweet' looks like a set phrase but splits between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A gumdrop is a chewy jelly sweet, a kind of confectionery.

clue.text: Any rent change will involve leader of these residents

indicators.note: will involve means the shuffled letters take in another letter
change means the letters of any rent are altered in order
leader of picks the first letter of the word these

explanation.surface: A rise in rent will affect the head of the household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' turns ANY RENT into TENANRY, which 'will involve' the T from 'leader of these'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenantry means tenants collectively, people who reside on rented land.

clue.text: Record details, aids to candidate cheating in exam?

definitions.meaning: the text printed on an LP or CD cover about the music and performers

definitions.text: aids to candidate cheating in exam?
definitions.meaning: crib notes hidden up a sleeve, read whimsically as notes from the sleeve

explanation.surface: Notes on an album cover double as a cheat's hidden crib in an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleeve notes are the written information on a record's cover, and literally notes tucked in a sleeve.

clue.text: Attendant, one dismissed by chief

indicators.note: dismissed means the numeral one is sent away from the word for chief

parts.note: main means chief, as in the main reason
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A servant is sacked by the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A man in the old sense is a servant or valet, as in manservant, so an attendant.

clue.text: Desert area has repulsed soldiers

indicators.note: repulsed means driven back, so the letters for area and has are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
RA, the Royal Artillery, stands for soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops are driven back in a desert region.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sahara is the largest hot desert, in North Africa, so an example of a desert.

clue.text: Press agent offering old-fashioned evening out?

definitions.text: Press agent offering old-fashioned evening out?

parts.words: Press agent offering old-fashioned evening out?
parts.note: not a publicist but an old tool for pressing clothes that evens out creases, the old heated metal kind

explanation.surface: A publicist proposes a quaint night on the town.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat iron is an old-fashioned heavy iron heated on a stove to press cloth smooth.

clue.text: Groom, miserable after cake

indicators.note: after puts the word for miserable behind the cake

parts.note: a sponge is a light cake
down means sad or miserable

explanation.surface: A bridegroom is upset after the wedding cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' is a verb, to clean, not the bridegroom.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponge down a horse or person is to wash and tidy, a sense of groom.

clue.text: Audibly criticising Times for present-day coverage?

indicators.note: Audibly says the word for criticising is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: rapping means criticising sharply, as in a rap on the knuckles
The Times is a newspaper, so a paper

explanation.surface: A newspaper is being loudly attacked for its coverage of modern affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present-day' means the day of giving presents: a birthday or Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrapping paper covers a present, read as coverage for a present on its special day.

clue.text: Prepare to broadcast over peak viewing period

parts.note: to prime is to prepare, as with a pump or a wall

indicators.note: over in a down clue means turned over, so the word for broadcast is read upwards

parts.note: to emit is to send out or broadcast

explanation.surface: Get ready to air across the busiest television slot.
explanation.definitionFit: Prime time is the evening slot with the largest television audience.

clue.text: Seafood could make you collapse in convulsions

indicators.note: in convulsions means thrown about violently, so the letters of collapse are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bad shellfish might leave you writhing on the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: An escallop, a variant of scallop, is a shellfish, an example of seafood.

clue.text: Mentioned first of two things a gambler needs, as a matter of course?

indicators.note: Mentioned first of says only the first of the pair is taken by sound, the second keeps its spelling

parts.note: a gambler needs a stake and chips to play

explanation.surface: Someone lists the basics a punter routinely requires.
explanation.walkthrough: Only STAKE is turned into its soundalike STEAK; 'course' is a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Steak and chips is a classic main dish, a matter of a meal's course.

clue.text: Obscure film excerpts shown in English language finally

indicators.note: shown in means the excerpts are displayed between the two other letters
finally picks the last letter of the word language

parts.note: clips are short excerpts from a film

explanation.surface: Unclear film snippets appear in an English-language programme.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse is to obscure, as the moon blocks the sun.

clue.text: Indian playwright born in France

parts.note: George Bernard Shaw was an Irish playwright
née is French for born, used for maiden names

explanation.surface: A dramatist of Indian heritage was born in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shawnee are a Native American people, so an Indian in the old American sense.

clue.text: After victory, I took charge, wearing disguise

indicators.note: After puts I and the word for took charge behind victory

parts.note: VE as in VE Day, Victory in Europe, 8 May 1945
led means took charge or was in command

explanation.surface: Once the war was won, I assumed command in disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Veiled means covered or concealed, as by a disguise.

clue.text: Nervous, having a bet

parts.note: a flutter is British slang for a small bet

explanation.surface: Someone is jittery after placing a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: Aflutter means in a state of nervous excitement, a synonym of nervous.

clue.text: Delicacy to eat in small amounts

definitions.meaning: refinement or discernment, good judgement in style
to sample food by trying a little

explanation.surface: A dainty dish should be nibbled sparingly.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste means refinement of judgement, and as a verb means to sample a little food.

clue.text: Soldiers found service a serious nuisance

parts.note: men are ordinary soldiers, the ranks
an ace is an unreturnable service in tennis

explanation.surface: Troops find that duty is a real pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A menace can mean a pest or an annoying person, so a serious nuisance.

clue.text: Bird outside's driven off by cat's mewing

indicators.note: outside's driven off means the outer letters of the phrase are removed to expose the middle run

explanation.surface: A garden bird flees when the cat starts mewing.
explanation.walkthrough: Take away the outside letters CA and ING from 'cat's mewing'.
explanation.definitionFit: The smew is a small diving duck, an example of a bird.

clue.text: European fails to complete circuit

indicators.note: fails to complete means the last letter of the word for European is left off

parts.note: a Lapp is a person from Lapland in northern Europe

explanation.surface: A European runner cannot finish the race.
explanation.definitionFit: A lap is one circuit of a racetrack, a synonym of circuit.

clue.text: Warning almost rings false

indicators.note: false means not genuine, so the letters of almost rings are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bells sounding not quite right give a false alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm signal is a warning flag or light showing that a storm is coming.

clue.text: Terribly pert, even for a twelve year old?

indicators.note: Terribly suggests the word pert is mangled into a new order

parts.note: e'en is the poetic contraction of even

explanation.surface: A cheeky child is very sassy, even at twelve.
explanation.definitionFit: Preteen describes a child just below thirteen; twelve-year-olds are an example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Small boy accompanies daughter for a couple of days

parts.note: wee is Scottish and informal for small
Ken is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A little lad goes with his daughter for two days.
explanation.definitionFit: A weekend is Saturday and Sunday, a couple of days.
